narrative.overview:
Girovo is a bank branch that opens for one person. Nothing on the walls sells anything, every figure is the bank's own, and the counter is tidy. The look is Material 3 Expressive, drawn by the real `@m3e/web` components (wrapped in `components/ui.tsx`), in Google Sans Flex, on Material You's wallpaper roles on an Android phone and on Girovo's own blue scheme everywhere else (`app/material.css`).

The phone is the system's reference. Its home has one field at the head that searches every booking, action and setting and, on Android, answers a question about the bookings. Below it the balance is set flat, then a row of chips, then the bookings, then three places at the foot. The page is flat and list-first; tone, weight and space carry the hierarchy, and the colours that carry a value never follow the wallpaper.

The desktop (from 640px) follows the phone later (owner, 2026-10-23: "don't update desktop yet"). It still has the two-pane Übersicht, the balance as a filled hero card, the navigation rail and the line icons; it inherits the colour rules below. Round two of the phone redesign (Material Symbols, wallpaper chart tones, the transitions, the transfer's two parts, the tabbed Umsatzdetails, the brand-field Anmeldung) is Android only: `IS_ANDROID` in code, `html[data-platform="android"]` in CSS.
keyCharacteristics: Search-first home: a 56dp search bar is the only tinted shape at the top.
A flat 48/500 balance with tight tracking; no balance card on the phone.
Three text sizes (12, 14, 16), one section step (18), one screen step (22), and display figures.
Weight 500 for emphasis on the phone; rank is weight and tone before size.
Owned value colours: green, red, amber and orange each mean one thing.
Three places, no FAB on the phone; Material Symbols Rounded, the current place filled.

rules.name: The Owned Colours Rule
rules.body: Green is a credit or a confirmation. Red is a negative balance or an error, never a debit: a debit is ink. A credit card's balance stays ink (a card is known by its Kontoart, `isCardAccount`). Amber means Vorgemerkt and nothing else; a warning is an orange glyph. Orange is never text.

rules.name: The Fixed Values Rule
rules.body: The value colours (including `chart-in` and `chart-out`), the brand plate, Plus Gold and Gemini's colours never take a wallpaper colour. Surfaces, ink, lines, the interactive colour and, on Android only, the six category slots and the rest follow Material You.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's default palette is switched off; every colour is a token. Literal colours exist only for literal things: the plates, a QR or TAN plate, the chipTAN flicker field.

rules.name: The Symbol Rule
rules.body: On Android every app icon is a Material Symbol (`Icon`'s `ms` name) in a box of exactly 1em, sized in dp: `text-size-adjust: none`, so the system's larger text grows the words, never the glyph. `filled` sets FILL 1, used only for the current place in the navigation bar (24px). Gemini's spark and the avatar glyphs are pictures and stay drawn. The desktop keeps the line icons (24 grid, 1.8 stroke).

rules.name: The Two Headings Rule
rules.body: A section is 18/500 in ink; a subheader is 14/500 in the variant ink. Einstellungen keeps its subheaders in the primary (owner, 2026-10-20). There is no third treatment.

rules.name: The Medium Weight Rule
rules.body: On the phone emphasis is 500, never 600 or 700. Rank comes from weight and tone before size.

rules.name: The Tight Figures Rule
rules.body: No positive tracking on figures. An amount is −0.01em; a display figure (`[data-balance]`, `[data-figure]`) is −0.025em. Body text keeps the face's own spacing (0).

rules.name: The Kontoauszug Column Rule
rules.body: Every amount goes through `<Money>`: tabular lining figures, a real minus (U+2212), and the privacy mask ("••• €") under Beträge ausblenden. Dates and counts take `.tnum`.

rules.name: The Character-by-Character Rule
rules.body: IBAN, BIC, BLZ and references are in Plex Mono. An IBAN gets 0.06em tracking and never wraps.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case, never capitals, on screen and on paper.

rules.name: The Reading Order Rule
rules.body: The DOM order is the narrow reading order. A wider layout places blocks with the grid, never with CSS `order`.

rules.name: The Phone's Page Rule
rules.body: On the phone's home the bookings are visible without scrolling. Whatever would push them down (summaries, the chart) goes behind a tap.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: A section on the page has no surface, corners, shadow or hairline between rows. The phone's page has no container at all; the desktop's one container is the balance hero. The exception is Einstellungen (owner, 2026-10-20): Material 3 Expressive's grouped list, rows as tiles on Container, 2px seams, 20px outer corners, 4px inner ones.

rules.name: The Scroll Edge Rule
rules.body: A pinned header or footer inside a sheet is flat while everything fits; a 1px hairline appears only once content runs under it.

rules.name: The Safe Choice Rule
rules.body: At every risk decision the safe action is the filled primary and the risky one the tonal button beside it. A destructive confirm the user asked for keeps its red button, with the safe one focused.

rules.name: The Safe Focus Rule
rules.body: A layer opens on the safe place (`safeFocusTarget`): what it names, else its first text field, else its close button, else the layer. Never a checkbox, switch, radio, link or action. A field marked `fine` takes focus only with a fine pointer, so a touch keyboard never covers a layer as it opens.

rules.name: The Pinned Way Out Rule
rules.body: A dialog's actions and a panel's closing action sit in a footer below the scrolling body and never scroll away.

rules.name: The Spring Rule
rules.body: Motion uses M3E's springs: spatial (position, size, shape) overshoots slightly; effects (colour, opacity) never do. `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured.

rules.name: The Backwards Fill Rule
rules.body: A page-level entrance animation uses `animation-fill-mode: backwards`, never `both` or `forwards`. A transform or opacity held after the animation ends creates a containing block and a stacking context, and the sheets and drawers that render in place inside it are trapped in the page instead of covering the screen.

rules.name: The Record Rule
rules.body: Paper prints the bank's words as the bank sent them. Where the sheet leads with a name the app derived, "Name laut Bank" prints the whole string beside it. A balance the bank did not send is marked "(errechnet)".

rules.name: The Third-Party Rule
rules.body: Paper speaks in the third person and carries only what its reader needs. A Buchungsbeleg never shows the account's balance, a logo, a note or a receipt.

rules.name: The Two-Sign Rule
rules.body: On paper a debit is ink and a credit green, and both signs are written out, so a grey copy says the same. A balance carries only its minus.

dos: **Do** reach for tokens by name (`text-ink-2`, `bg-inset`, `var(--nav-bg)`) so the theme and Material You resolve themselves.
**Do** put the look in `app/material.css` and only what a phone needs in `app/android.css` behind `data-platform="android"`.
**Do** route every amount through `<Money>` and every IBAN through `.iban`.
**Do** keep the phone to 12, 14, 16, 18 and 22 plus the display figures (48 for the balance, 32 to 36 for a lead).
**Do** use the two heading treatments: 18/500 ink for a section, 14/500 variant ink for a subheader.
**Do** keep the bookings visible on the phone's first screen; put charts and summaries behind a tap.
**Do** give charts colours by rank (top six, rest grey), green for income and navy-slate for spending.
**Do** give every new Android icon an `ms` name from Material Symbols Rounded and add it to the subset.
**Do** use the spaced Gedankenstrich (" – ") and German quotes („…“) in interface strings.
donts: **Don't** colour a debit red, or a credit card's balance.
**Don't** use amber for anything but Vorgemerkt, or orange as text.
**Don't** let a value colour, a chart slot, a plate or Gemini's colours follow Material You.
**Don't** use 600 or 700 on the phone, or positive tracking on a figure.
**Don't** put a card, a shadow or a hairline grid on the page to group a section (Einstellungen's grouped list excepted).
**Don't** float a FAB over the phone's bookings or add a fourth place to the navigation.
**Don't** bring back an outlined secondary button.
**Don't** fill a chart area with a gradient.
**Don't** hold a page-level animation's end state (`forwards` or `both`).
**Don't** let the icons scale with the system's text size, or fill any icon but the current place.
**Don't** use any bank's logo or name as the app's own identity.
